platform: Same Apple M1 as the previous secured and old direct125M measurements

measurement.scope: Serial warm-cache fresh-process spawn through observed child exit including secured CLI acquisition/output/report; standard Rust1ms polling. Build, hashing and parent validation excluded; not kernel or cold-cache timing.

comparison.scope: Whole implementation difference, not isolated capability overhead. Old code used packed lowering, compact counters and four partitions. All comparisons here use the same full125M input on this M1.

implementation: Generic instruction selection for the already-proved canonical String window-query region. No alphabet, source, name or hash specialization and no full benchmark helper.

Widths1..7 pack only the actual query bytes, then compare masked little-endian source words only while offset<=length-8. The original bounded byte loop handles at most7 tail starts and all sources shorter than8 bytes.

Widths>=8 compare a cached8-byte query prefix before the ordinary byte remainder. Width/query-length/owner bounds precede every load; there are no aligned, notrap or can_move assertions. Invalid widths return0 before loads.

All overlapping starts and exact String semantics remain. Real admitted owners, ASCII/noCRLF proof with canonical fallback, finite complete-region bounds, cumulative accounts, original errors and atomic publication within one host round are unchanged.
No new allocation, unsafe code, ABI/control-IR/work-policy contract, authority or renewed allowance. Actual generated code/stack size and immutable Object pins are still derived/checked.

The following lint-only emitter refactor groups the four byte-loop CFG blocks in a private ByteLoop struct and removes the exception. It does not change emitted instruction order, bounds or runtime protocol; this timing remains attributed to e482, not that later revision.
